note: Time-indexed meter graph. nodes and meters are fixed throughout (the 22 meters in meter-number order, as in graph_meters.json). graphs holds one edge set per distinct wiring; graph 0 is the reference (nominal) wiring and equals graph_meters.json. periods are half-open in time; each names its graph and carries each meter's merged bus set and component in that period. Times in start and end are in the switch files' fixed-PST base; start_utc and end_utc_exclusive are seconds since 1970 UTC. The wiring in force at a time is the period holding it. Which graph a forecast window uses is decided by the data side (the graph at its last history slot). Electrical weights (main_electricalweights.py): admittance_abs on every edge is the magnitude of the pair's entry in the per-unit positive-sequence nodal admittance matrix of the period's network, assembled from the complete terminal blocks of graph.json (shunt parts, transformer ratios and phase shifts included) and Kron-reduced onto the metered nodes, divided by the largest value of its edge set; two meters on one node carry 1.0. It is a scalar coupling measure, not an electrical equivalent of the network: it is positive-sequence only and a magnitude does not carry the angle of the reduced entry. Connections are unchanged from the source file.

weights.scaling: per edge set: divided by its largest weight; same-node pairs 1.0
left_out: the angle of the reduced entry
off_nominal: tr_127: winding rated 2.46 kV on a 2.401 kV bus (ratio 1.0247)
tr_128: winding rated 2.46 kV on a 2.401 kV bus (ratio 1.0247)

comparison.what: series-only approximation (lines by their series part, transformers from the nameplate with no ratio and no phase shift); not stored in this file
